skill.name: analysis-tshark
skill.description: Guide for authorized TShark and Wireshark command-line packet capture, traffic inspection, protocol analysis, and network forensic workflows.
skill.summary: Analyze packet captures and live traffic with TShark for authorized security investigations.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, defensive templates, or reference examples. Confirmed risks remain for privileged packet capture, TLS key material handling, credential extraction workflows, wireless/interface enumeration, shell automation, and a CI curl-to-bash installer pattern.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with a pinned package release, checksum verification, or a reviewed action version.

remediation.issue: Live packet capture and setup examples rely on sudo or elevated capabilities.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger guardrails for authorization, scope, least privilege, and rollback of group or capability changes.

remediation.issue: Credential extraction workflows can expose passwords, hashes, cookies, and authentication data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit investigative purpose, redact outputs by default, and document retention and destruction steps.

remediation.issue: TLS decryption examples require SSL key logs or private server keys.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to store key material separately, restrict access, and delete temporary decryption artifacts after review.

remediation.issue: The monitoring script emails captured network metadata automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Make recipients configurable, redact sensitive fields, and require approval before sending capture-derived data.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Extraction Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill explicitly guides extraction of HTTP Basic authentication, FTP passwords, NTLM hashes, SMTP authentication, POP3 credentials, and IMAP logins from captures. This is valid for authorized forensics but creates high risk if used outside a defined investigation scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The section is titled credential extraction and contains direct workflows for multiple credential types. The surrounding text limits use to authorized forensics, but the capability is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Packet Capture of Sensitive Traffic
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs live packet capture with elevated privileges and notes that captures can expose sensitive information. Broad packet capture can collect third-party traffic, credentials, and personal data if scope controls are weak.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source repeatedly requires authorization and secure storage, which confirms the author understands the sensitivity. The live capture commands require elevated access and can collect broad traffic.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Alert Email May Expose Capture Metadata

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script explicitly logs and emails captured network fields. The destination is a placeholder SOC address, so the risk depends on deployment context.

content.value_statement: Security teams need repeatable ways to inspect packet captures without opening a full desktop tool. This skill guides authorized TShark workflows for traffic analysis, forensic triage, and protocol evidence review.
actual_capabilities: Guides live packet capture and pcap file review with TShark commands.
Shows display filters for HTTP, DNS, TLS, SMB, email, and wireless traffic.
Explains how to extract protocol fields, artifacts, credentials, and indicators from captures.
Provides workflows for malware traffic analysis, incident response, and network forensics.
Includes operational guidance for storage, access control, retention, and chain of custody.
limitations: Requires TShark or Wireshark command-line tools installed on the host system.
Live capture often requires elevated privileges and explicit network monitoring authorization.
Encrypted traffic cannot be inspected without authorized key material or endpoint logs.
Large captures may require careful filtering, storage planning, and manual validation.

use_cases.title: Investigate Security Incidents
use_cases.description: Review packet captures for suspicious hosts, beaconing, failed connections, and possible data transfer patterns.

use_cases.title: Validate Network Controls
use_cases.description: Check whether sensitive protocols, weak encryption, or unexpected traffic appear in monitored environments.

use_cases.title: Prepare Forensic Evidence
use_cases.description: Extract timelines, protocol fields, files, and indicators from captures while preserving documentation quality.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the TShark skill to help me inspect this pcap for top protocols, endpoints, DNS queries, and unusual HTTP activity.

prompt_templates.title: Build Display Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Create TShark display filters for suspected credential exposure across HTTP, FTP, POP3, IMAP, SMB, and NTLM traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Malware Traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a malware traffic review with TShark. Focus on beaconing, DNS anomalies, payload downloads, and outbound data movement.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Forensic Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn TShark findings into a concise forensic report with timeline notes, indicators, confidence, and data handling cautions.

output_examples.input: A SOC analyst asks for first-pass pcap triage.
output: A prioritized review plan covering endpoints, protocols, DNS, HTTP, and connection failures.
Suggested TShark filters for each question and notes about sensitive data handling.

output_examples.input: An incident responder suspects malware beaconing.
output: A focused workflow to compare timing, destinations, user agents, DNS names, and payload activity.
A short findings outline that separates confirmed indicators from items needing validation.

output_examples.input: A security engineer needs to validate TLS visibility.
output: Guidance on what TShark can show without keys and what requires authorized key material.
Warnings about protecting key logs, private keys, and decrypted capture outputs.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before live packet capture.
Use narrow filters and short durations to reduce sensitive data collection.
Encrypt capture files and restrict access to analysts with a clear need.
anti_patterns: Do not capture broad network traffic without a defined investigation scope.
Do not extract or store credentials unless the investigation explicitly requires it.
Do not share raw captures or decrypted traffic without redaction and approval.

faq.question: Does this skill run TShark by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and commands that a user or agent can apply in an authorized environment.

faq.question: Can it inspect encrypted traffic?
faq.answer: Only limited metadata is visible unless authorized key logs or private keys are available.

faq.question: Is live packet capture safe to use?
faq.answer: It is sensitive. Use it only with documented authorization, narrow scope, and secure storage.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflows assume TShark or Wireshark command-line tools. Some tasks may also use common shell utilities.

faq.question: Can this help with incident reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure findings, indicators, timelines, and evidence notes from packet analysis.

faq.question: Does it replace analyst judgment?
faq.answer: No. Packet evidence needs context, validation, and careful handling of sensitive data.
